prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1091; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Signs point to a set-up crash: the front car braked hard for no reason and the people in both cars knew each other.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a rear-end collision in a parking lot and said they hit their head on the steering wheel, with symptoms of a concussion. The reported injury is consistent with the impact described.

Entry 2: Claimant contacted the office and has no legal representation. They gave the same account of the collision as on the first report and said they were seated in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: Police and two witnesses at the scene confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle when the collision occurred. The damage to the claimant's vehicle matches the impact described, and no earlier damage to it is known.

Entry 4: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the coverage was in force on the day of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 5: The driver of the claimant's vehicle lives in the policyholder's household and is covered as a household member. No earlier injury to the same area of the head or neck appears in the medical history.

Entry 6: The front vehicle's driver braked sharply with no apparent reason, and the statements show the two drivers knew each other. These details point toward a set-up collision, and the file is being referred for further review.

Entry 7: Treatment has grown well beyond what is typical for this injury, with more visits and new services added each month. The medical bills and therapy notes are being reviewed against the expected course of recovery.

Entry 8: Claimant continues to report the same account and symptoms in each conversation. The file remains open pending the review of the treatment records and the outcome of the referral.
